title: Jeremiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Jeremiah chapter 39 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Jeremiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Jeremiah Chapter 39.

questions.question: In which year of Zedekiah king of Judah did Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon come against Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:1 states that in the ninth year of Zedekiah king of Judah, Nebuchadrezzar king of Babylon came against Jerusalem.

questions.question: During which month did Nebuchadrezzar besiege Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:1 specifies that Nebuchadrezzar besieged Jerusalem in the tenth month.

questions.question: On what day of the month was the city broken up in the eleventh year of Zedekiah?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:2 states that the city was broken up on the ninth day of the fourth month in the eleventh year of Zedekiah.

questions.question: Where did the princes of the king of Babylon sit when they came into Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:3 mentions that the princes of the king of Babylon sat in the middle gate after entering the city.

questions.question: How did Zedekiah king of Judah escape from Jerusalem?
options: By night, by the way of the king's garden
questions.correctAnswer: By night, by the way of the king's garden
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:4 describes how Zedekiah fled by night through the king's garden and the gate between the two walls.

questions.question: Where was Zedekiah overtaken by the Chaldeans?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:5 says the Chaldeans overtook Zedekiah in the plains of Jericho.

questions.question: What happened to Zedekiah's sons before his eyes?
options: They were slain by the king of Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: They were slain by the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:6 states that the king of Babylon slew the sons of Zedekiah before his eyes.

questions.question: True or False: The king of Babylon put out Zedekiah's eyes after capturing him.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:7 explains that the king of Babylon put out Zedekiah's eyes.

questions.question: True or False: The Chaldeans spared the walls of Jerusalem after capturing the city.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:8 shows that the Chaldeans broke down the walls of Jerusalem.

questions.question: Who took captive the remnant of the people remaining in the city and carried them away to Babylon?
options: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:9 states that Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard carried away captive the remnant of the people into Babylon.

questions.question: What did Nebuzaradan do with the poor of the land of Judah?
options: Left them in the land and gave them vineyards and fields
questions.correctAnswer: Left them in the land and gave them vineyards and fields
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:10 describes how Nebuzaradan left the poor in the land and gave them vineyards and fields.

questions.question: Who was given charge over Jeremiah to ensure he was treated well?
options: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.correctAnswer: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:11-12 states that Nebuchadrezzar gave charge to Nebuzaradan concerning Jeremiah to look well to him and do no harm.

questions.question: To whom was Jeremiah delivered after being taken out of prison?
options: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:14 says Jeremiah was committed to Gedaliah the son of Ahikam after being taken from prison.

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah while he was free in the city.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:15 states the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah while he was shut up in the court of the prison.

questions.question: Who was Jeremiah instructed to speak to regarding the coming evil upon the city?
options: Nebuzaradan the captain of the guard
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:16 directs Jeremiah to speak to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian about the impending evil upon the city.

medium.title: Jeremiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Jeremiah Chapter 39 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What happened to King Zedekiah after he was captured by the Chaldeans?
options: He was put to death immediately
He was put out his eyes and bound with chains
He was released to rule another city
He was made a servant in Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He was put out his eyes and bound with chains
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:7 states that the king of Babylon put out Zedekiah's eyes and bound him with chains to carry him to Babylon, showing his harsh treatment after capture.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 39, what did the Chaldeans do to Jerusalem after capturing it?
options: They burned the king's house and broke down the walls
questions.correctAnswer: They burned the king's house and broke down the walls
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:8 describes how the Chaldeans burned the king's house and the houses of the people and broke down the walls of Jerusalem, reflecting total destruction.

questions.question: Who did Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, carry away captive into Babylon?
options: The remnant of the people that remained in the city
questions.correctAnswer: The remnant of the people that remained in the city
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:9 tells us Nebuzaradan carried away captive the remnant of the people remaining in the city, including those who had defected to him, indicating a selective captivity.

questions.question: What did Nebuzaradan do with the poor people who had nothing in Judah?
options: He took them captive to Babylon
He left them in the land and gave them vineyards and fields
He expelled them from the land
He made them servants to Babylonian nobles
questions.correctAnswer: He left them in the land and gave them vineyards and fields
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:10 explains that Nebuzaradan left the poor of the people in Judah and gave them vineyards and fields, showing mercy and provision for the destitute.

questions.question: What specific instructions did Nebuchadrezzar give concerning Jeremiah?
options: To keep him safe and do no harm to him
To send him back to Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: To keep him safe and do no harm to him
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:11-12 records Nebuchadrezzar's charge to Nebuzaradan to take care of Jeremiah, look well to him, and do him no harm, indicating God's protection over Jeremiah.

questions.question: How does the treatment of Jeremiah in captivity teach us about God's care for His servants?
options: God abandons His servants in captivity
God ensures His servants suffer like everyone else
God commands captors to protect and obey His servants
God ignores the fate of His servants
questions.correctAnswer: God commands captors to protect and obey His servants
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:11-12 shows God’s instruction through Nebuchadrezzar to protect Jeremiah and do him no harm, teaching believers that God cares deeply for those who trust Him.

questions.question: Where was Jeremiah placed after being released from the prison court?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:14 records that Jeremiah was entrusted to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, and dwelt among the people, highlighting a measure of freedom and community.

questions.question: What assurance did God give to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian through Jeremiah?
options: He would be killed by the sword
He would be handed over to his enemies
He would be delivered and not fall by the sword
He would be exiled to Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: He would be delivered and not fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:17-18 promises Ebedmelech that he would be delivered and not fall by the sword because he put his trust in God, showing faith's protective power.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 39 teach about the virtue of trust in God during difficult times?
options: Trust leads to certain earthly success
Trust in God brings deliverance despite danger
Trust is irrelevant in times of trouble
questions.correctAnswer: Trust in God brings deliverance despite danger
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:18 illustrates that trusting God results in deliverance from harm, even when facing deadly threats, encouraging believers to rely on God's protection.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 39 reveal about God's justice through the fate of Zedekiah and his sons?
options: God rewards the king with riches
God allows the king's sons to rule
God executes judgment by the king of Babylon
God rescues Zedekiah and his family
questions.correctAnswer: God executes judgment by the king of Babylon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:6 shows that Nebuchadnezzar slew Zedekiah's sons and nobles before his eyes, reflecting God's judgment on Judah for disobedience.

questions.question: According to Jeremiah 39, what route did Zedekiah take when he fled Jerusalem?
options: The king's garden and the gate between two walls
questions.correctAnswer: The king's garden and the gate between two walls
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:4 describes Zedekiah fleeing by night via the king's garden and the gate between two walls, showing his attempt to escape unnoticed.

questions.question: True or False: Nebuzaradan left only the wealthy people in Judah and took away the poor to Babylon.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:10 states that Nebuzaradan left the poor people who had nothing in the land of Judah and gave them vineyards and fields, contradicting the statement.

questions.question: True or False: Nebuchadrezzar ordered that Jeremiah be treated with care and obeyed in all things.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:11-12 records Nebuchadrezzar's command to Nebuzaradan to take Jeremiah and do no harm to him but obey whatever he said, showing special care.

questions.question: True or False: The word of the LORD came to Jeremiah while he was free in the city of Jerusalem.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:15 states that the word of the LORD came to Jeremiah while he was shut up in the court of the prison, not free in the city.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 39 teach about how God rewards those who put their trust in Him, based on Ebedmelech's example?
options: They will be delivered from enemies and danger
They will be exempt from all punishment
questions.correctAnswer: They will be delivered from enemies and danger
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:17-18 promises deliverance and protection to Ebedmelech because he trusted in God, teaching that faith brings divine rescue amid hardships.

hard.title: Jeremiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Jeremiah Chapter 39.

questions.question: Who was Jeremiah entrusted to after being taken out of the prison courtyard?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was committed unto Gedaliah, the son of Ahikam, to carry him home and dwell among the people as stated in Jeremiah 39:14.

questions.question: What specific instruction did Nebuchadrezzar give regarding Jeremiah's treatment?
options: Do him no harm and do as he commands
Execute him at the king's discretion
questions.correctAnswer: Do him no harm and do as he commands
questions.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar instructed Nebuzaradan to take care of Jeremiah and do no harm to him, but to do as Jeremiah said (Jeremiah 39:12).

questions.question: Which officials were sent by Nebuzaradan to retrieve Jeremiah from prison?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:13 lists these specific princes of the king of Babylon sent by Nebuzaradan to bring Jeremiah out of prison.

questions.question: What was the LORD’s message to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian while Jeremiah was imprisoned?
options: The city will face evil, not good, and it will happen soon
The city will be spared and prosper
Ebedmelech will be king of Judah
questions.correctAnswer: The city will face evil, not good, and it will happen soon
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:16 records God's word to speak to Ebedmelech that the city will suffer evil, not good, and it will be fulfilled in his time.

questions.question: What promise did God give to Ebedmelech regarding his safety?
options: He will be delivered and not fall by the sword
He will be taken captive to Babylon
He will be made king of Judah
He will be blinded like Zedekiah
questions.correctAnswer: He will be delivered and not fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:17-18 assure Ebedmelech that he will be delivered from his enemies and his life will be preserved because he trusted in God.

questions.question: What literary device is demonstrated by the parallel mention of Nebuzaradan, Nebushasban, Rabsaris, Nergalsharezer, and Rabmag in verses 13 and 3?
options: Inclusio, framing the narrative with repeated names
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio, framing the narrative with repeated names
questions.explanation: The repetition of these Babylonian officials at the siege’s start (v3) and in the retrieval of Jeremiah (v13) creates an inclusio framing the narrative, emphasizing Babylonian authority (Jeremiah 39:3, 39:13).

questions.question: What is the significance of the name "Ebedmelech," especially in the context of Jeremiah 39:16-18?
options: "Servant of the king," indicating his role and trust in God
questions.correctAnswer: "Servant of the king," indicating his role and trust in God
questions.explanation: Ebedmelech means 'servant of the king' in Hebrew, highlighting his position in the palace and his faithfulness, which God honors by promising deliverance (Jeremiah 39:16-18).

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 39:15-18 foreshadow New Testament themes of trust and deliverance?
options: By showing trust in God leads to salvation, echoing Jesus' teaching in John 14:1
By predicting a physical kingdom established by the Messiah
By focusing on political power and conquest
questions.correctAnswer: By showing trust in God leads to salvation, echoing Jesus' teaching in John 14:1
questions.explanation: The promise to Ebedmelech that trusting God leads to deliverance parallels Jesus’ exhortation to trust in Him for peace and salvation (John 14:1), illustrating continuity of divine faithfulness (Jeremiah 39:17-18; John 14:1).

questions.question: Which earlier book of the Bible contains a prophecy about Nebuchadnezzar's judgment that is fulfilled in Jeremiah 39?
questions.explanation: The Book of Daniel foretells Nebuchadnezzar’s role in God's judgment on Jerusalem, which is fulfilled historically as described in Jeremiah 39:5-8 with the capture of Zedekiah and destruction of Jerusalem.

questions.question: What historical and cultural context explains why Nebuchadnezzar would blind King Zedekiah after his capture?
options: Blinding was a common practice to prevent a captive king from ruling or escaping
It was a ritual to honor defeated kings
To prepare the king for a Babylonian religious ceremony
To make the king a prophet for Babylon
questions.correctAnswer: Blinding was a common practice to prevent a captive king from ruling or escaping
questions.explanation: According to Jeremiah 39:7, Nebuchadnezzar blinded Zedekiah to incapacitate him politically and physically, a common ancient Near Eastern practice to secure conquered rulers.

questions.question: How does the treatment of the poor left in Judah by Nebuzaradan connect to themes of social justice in the Bible?
options: They were left with vineyards and fields, showing God's care for the vulnerable
They were forced into military service
questions.correctAnswer: They were left with vineyards and fields, showing God's care for the vulnerable
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:10 notes that Nebuzaradan left the poor in the land and gave them vineyards and fields, reflecting biblical concern for the disadvantaged (cf. Deuteronomy 15:7-11).

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of prophetic imprisonment and divine communication found in Jeremiah 39:15?
questions.explanation: Acts 16:25-34 recounts Paul and Silas praying and receiving God’s message while imprisoned, paralleling Jeremiah’s receipt of God’s word in prison (Jeremiah 39:15).

questions.question: True or False: Zedekiah was captured in the city of Jerusalem during the Babylonian siege.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:4-5 explains that Zedekiah fled the city by night but was captured in the plains of Jericho, not within Jerusalem itself.

questions.question: True or False: Nebuzaradan executed all the people who remained in Jerusalem after the siege.
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:9-10 states that Nebuzaradan took captive the remnant but left the poor in the land with vineyards and fields, so not all were executed.

questions.question: What was the fate of Zedekiah’s sons according to Jeremiah 39?
options: They were slain before his eyes by Nebuchadnezzar
They were exiled to Babylon as captives
questions.correctAnswer: They were slain before his eyes by Nebuchadnezzar
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 39:6 records that Nebuchadnezzar killed Zedekiah's sons in Riblah before Zedekiah's eyes as part of his judgment.

theological.title: Jeremiah Chapter 39 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Jeremiah Chapter 39 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What year of Zedekiah's reign did Nebuchadrezzar come against Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar came against Jerusalem in the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, as stated in Jeremiah 39:1.

questions.question: What happened to the city of Jerusalem in the eleventh year of Zedekiah?
questions.explanation: The city was broken up in the eleventh year of Zedekiah, as mentioned in Jeremiah 39:2.

questions.question: Who were the nobles that Nebuchadrezzar slew in Riblah?
questions.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar slew the sons of Zedekiah in Riblah before his eyes, as stated in Jeremiah 39:6.

questions.question: What did Nebuzaradan give to the poor of the people left in Judah?
questions.explanation: Nebuzaradan left the poor of the people and gave them vineyards and fields, as mentioned in Jeremiah 39:10.

questions.question: What instruction did Nebuchadrezzar give regarding Jeremiah?
questions.explanation: Nebuchadrezzar instructed Nebuzaradan to look well to Jeremiah and do him no harm, according to Jeremiah 39:12.

questions.question: What comfort does the Lord provide to Ebedmelech the Ethiopian?
questions.explanation: The Lord promises to deliver Ebedmelech on that day, as stated in Jeremiah 39:17.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 39:10 reveal about God's provision?
questions.explanation: The provision of vineyards and fields to the poor indicates God's care and provision for the needy, as seen in Jeremiah 39:10.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 39:4 illustrate Zedekiah's response to crisis?
questions.explanation: Zedekiah fled the city by night when he saw the Chaldean army, as described in Jeremiah 39:4.

questions.question: What phrase does the Lord use to describe the fate of Jerusalem in Jeremiah 39:16?
options: For good and not for evil
For evil and not for good
questions.correctAnswer: For evil and not for good
questions.explanation: The Lord states He will bring His words upon the city for evil and not for good, as indicated in Jeremiah 39:16.

questions.question: What does Jeremiah 39:18 indicate about trust in the Lord?
options: It brings peace to the city
questions.explanation: The verse states that because Ebedmelech put his trust in the Lord, he would not fall by the sword and would be delivered, as seen in Jeremiah 39:18.

questions.question: What event does Jeremiah 39:8 describe regarding Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: The Chaldeans burned the king's house and the houses of the people, which is described in Jeremiah 39:8.

questions.question: What doctrinal insight can be drawn from Jeremiah 39:7 and 39:6 regarding God's judgment?
questions.explanation: The execution of judgment on Zedekiah's sons and nobles shows that God's judgment is definitive and executed as stated in Jeremiah 39:6-7.

questions.question: What attribute of God is highlighted in Jeremiah 39:17 regarding Ebedmelech's situation?
questions.explanation: The promise of deliverance to Ebedmelech illustrates God's mercy in saving those who trust Him, as noted in Jeremiah 39:17.

questions.question: How does Jeremiah 39:14 connect Jeremiah's situation to God's plan?
options: He was restored to the people
He was punished for his prophecies
questions.correctAnswer: He was restored to the people
questions.explanation: Jeremiah was taken out of prison and committed to Gedaliah, indicating his restoration among the people, as seen in Jeremiah 39:14.

questions.question: How do Jeremiah 39:12 and 39:13 reflect the authority of the king of Babylon?
options: He is a servant of God
questions.explanation: The king of Babylon's orders regarding Jeremiah and the actions of his princes demonstrate his authority and power, as seen in Jeremiah 39:12-13.
